title: Detect JSON schema regressions in structured output evals
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a detection and alerting pipeline to catch quality regressions that break structured JSON outputs against expected schemas when models or serving configs change. Focus is on automated evals (offline and streaming) that validate per-field adherence (required presence, type, format) and surface regressions tied to specific model/config commits or rollout steps. The detector should distinguish hard schema violations (missing required fields / invalid types) from soft semantic drift (unexpected values but valid type), and provide per-field pass rates, example counterfactuals and links to failing traces to aid debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Automated eval harness uses canonical JSON schemas to validate outputs for at least three production routes (chat-structured, completion-to-JSON, and embedding-metadata) in nightly runs
Per-field pass/fail metrics and aggregate schema compliance rate appear in a Console dashboard with a 90-day timeseries
Regression alerting triggers when schema compliance drops by >5 percentage points vs baseline for a route after a model or config change; alerts include changelist/commit and failing examples
Integration test that runs against model canaries and fails a canary rollout when critical-schema-violation rate >0.5%
Documentation with schema authoring guidance and examples published in Confluence and linked from Console
tech_notes: We will reuse Ajv (Node) and python jsonschema for dual-run validation in the eval harness. Instrumentation will emit per-field counts (required_missing, type_mismatch, format_error, extra_fields) along with example generation. To tie regressions to changes, the eval runner will record model version, runtime config (batching, quantization profile), and rollout metadata; diffs will be computed between baseline job and current job. Trade-offs: strict schemas catch regressions early but produce false positives for intentionally changing outputs — we will support schema versioning and a tolerance window. Cost: nightly full-eval runs estimated at ~2x current token budget for affected routes; mitigate with sampling and prefix caching. Alerting: integrate with existing Console alerting and Slack channel #quality-regressions; critical alerts create a PagerDuty incident for P0 routes. Rollout policy: on detection, canary rollback or auto-fallback to previous model variant if severity exceeds thresholds.
implementation_plan: Week 1: schema collection & canonicalization — gather existing JSON output examples and draft canonical schemas with PM/Design
Week 2: eval harness instrumentation — add Ajv/jsonschema checks and per-field counters to eval runner; emit metrics to metrics pipeline
Week 3: dashboard and alerting — build Console widgets, threshold rules, and Slack/PagerDuty integrations
Week 4: canary gating and automation — wire regression checks into rollout pipeline and add automated rollback policy
Week 5: documentation & rollout — publish guidance, run cross-team dry-run, tune thresholds based on false-positive rate
